title: Cap. 7 Rat. 10: Augustine De corrept. & grat. 11—grace in Christ makes us will
pass_a_gloss: It also conflicts with the judgment of the orthodox Fathers who opposed the Pelagians, and namely of Augustine, On Rebuke and Grace chapter 11, where when he had shown of what sort that grace was which was given to the first Adam, concerning the grace prepared and given to the predestinate in Christ he speaks thus: So much more largely is the help of grace given through Jesus Christ to those to whom it pleased God to give it, that it not only is present without which we cannot remain, even if we should will, but also is so great and of such a kind that we will. For there is in us through this grace of God, in receiving the good and perseveringly holding it, not only to be able to do what we will, but also to will what we are able.
pass_b_english: It also clashes with the orthodox Fathers who opposed the Pelagians—above all Augustine, On Rebuke and Grace chapter 11. After showing what grace was given to the first Adam, he says of the grace prepared and given to the predestinate in Christ: “So much more largely is the help of grace given through Jesus Christ to those to whom God was pleased to give it, that it not only is present—without which we cannot remain even if we will—but also is so great and of such a kind that we will. For through this grace of God, in receiving the good and holding it perseveringly, there is in us not only the ability to do what we will, but also the will to do what we can.”
source_text: Repugnat etiam orthodoxorum Patrum sententiae, qui Pelagianis sese opposuerunt, ac nominatim Augustini, De corrept. & grat. cap. 11. ubi cum ostendisset, qualis ea gratia fuerit quae primo Adamo data fuit, De gratia praedestinatis in Christo praeparata & donata sic loquitur, Tanto amplius datur adjutorium gratiae per Jesum Christum, quibus id dare Deo placuit, ut non solum adsit sine quo permanere non possumus, etiamsi velimus, verum etiam tantum ac tale sit ut velimus. Est quippe in nobis per hanc Dei gratiam in bono recipiendo & perseveranter tenendo non solum posse quod volumus, verum etiam velle quod possumus.
